proposals.title: KC Border, The Second Welfare Theorem (January 2001; version 26 January 2016)
proposals.use: Full eight-page note: second-welfare valuation support statement, Scitovsky/resource sums, local-nonsatiation closure, relative continuity and alternative convexity definitions.
proposals.verification: Actual primary body scope inspected by ito_author; precise text/image/access limits retained.
limits: The note invokes separation without proving the needed open/noncompact theorem. The chapter supplies that input independently.

Strict contours are relatively open in X; they need not be ambient-open for arbitrary convex X. The chapter separates their convex sum from the ambient interior of the free-disposal resource set instead.
The note calls the semistrict mixture condition convex and distinguishes weak convexity; the chapter explicitly uses convex weak upper contours and proves convexity of strict contours directly.
The chapter supplies the omitted cheaper-bundle upgrade, nonnegative-price/disposal proof and ownership-balanced transfers. No source example is copied.

proposals.title: Daron Acemoglu, MIT 6.254 Guest Lecture: Social Choice and Voting Theory (6 May 2010)
proposals.use: Weak-order domain, Pareto, IIA, finite Arrow statement and decisive-coalition proof; Condorcet and single-peaked median definitions and proof.
proposals.verification: Actual primary body scope inspected by ito_author; precise text/image/access limits retained.
limits: Arrow proof reconstructed independently with explicit almost-versus-strong decisiveness and every three-alternative propagation step. No fourth alternative is required.

Slide 18 names the reduced coalition decisive between p2 and p3 in the branch with social p3 strictly above p2; its winning orientation is p3 over p2. The chapter uses an explicitly oriented partition table.

Slide 29 states the supporting coalition with peaks strictly above the median; the median itself and coincident peaks must be included using peaks at least the median. The chapter handles these counts explicitly.
Social ties are allowed; the minimal-coalition proof retains the weak reverse branch. Dictatorship constrains strict dictator comparisons, not the treatment of that voter’s indifferences.
No Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem, agenda equilibrium or strategy-proofness extension is used or claimed proved.

proposals.title: Robert M. Townsend, MIT 14.04: Lecture 16, Fundamental Welfare Theorems (Fall 2020), official transcript
proposals.use: Primary lecture content on the finite first-theorem value proof, smooth supporting-price and wealth-transfer construction, and the weaker consumer condition in price quasiequilibrium.
proposals.verification: Retrieved the actual 14-page official transcript. Inspected pages 2–4 on weakly preferred bundle costs, LNS, firm profit maximization and the feasibility contradiction; pages 5–10 on smooth planner/consumer/firm conditions and ownership-consistent transfers; and pages 11–12 on the quasiequilibrium inequality and convex separation route. The manuscript states its finite-dimensional assumptions explicitly, proves only its restricted constructive decentralization result and cheaper-bundle upgrade, and does not claim the general separation theorem or graduate infinite-dimensional proof has been supplied. The source's verbal slips and loose equivalence between utility concavity and preference regularity are not adopted. No source empirical illustration or exercise is copied.
proposals.disposition: Reuse existing catalogue ID and historical inspected scope; no fresh body/image claim
